short: His single-handed translation of the Bible into Latin became Western Christianity's standard text.
full:
Born around 347 in Dalmatia, Jerome studied in Rome, lived for years as an ascetic in the Syrian desert, and served as secretary to Pope Damasus I before settling in Bethlehem, where he ran a monastery until his death. Damasus had commissioned him to revise the existing Latin Gospels against the Greek text; Jerome expanded the project into a full translation of the Old Testament directly from Hebrew rather than the Greek Septuagint most earlier Latin versions relied on, a controversial choice he defended at length.

He completed the bulk of the translation, later known as the Vulgate, around 405, after roughly two decades of work alongside a vast output of commentaries, letters and polemic, including a running dispute with Augustine over translation method. The Vulgate only gradually displaced older Latin versions but became the standard Bible of Western Christianity for over a thousand years, shaping Latin theological vocabulary long after Jerome's death in 420.
